## Limits

1. Evaluate:
$$
\lim_{x\to -3}(x^2+4x-5)
$$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\lim_{x\to -3}(x^2+4x-5) = (-3)^2+4(-3)-5 = 9-12-5 = -8
$$
:::

2. Does the following limit exist? (Hint: Expand first)
$$
\lim_{x\to 4}\frac{(x-1)^2}{(x-1)}
$$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
Simplify first: $\frac{(x-1)^2}{(x-1)}=\frac{(x-1)(x-1)}{(x-1)}=x-1$ for $x\neq 1$.

$$
\lim_{x\to 4}(x-1) = 3
$$

The limit **exists** and equals $3$.
:::

3. Does the following limit exist?
$$
\lim_{x\to 5}\frac{2}{x-5}
$$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
Approaching from the right ($x>5$): $x-5\to 0^+$, so $\frac{2}{x-5}\to +\infty$.

Approaching from the left ($x<5$): $x-5\to 0^-$, so $\frac{2}{x-5}\to -\infty$.

Since the function approaches different (infinite) behavior from the left and right, the limit **does not exist**.
:::

4. Let
$$
g(x)=\begin{cases}2x-3, & x\geq 1\\x-2, & x<1\end{cases}
$$
Does the following limit exist?
$$
\lim_{x\to 1}g(x)
$$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
Approaching from the right ($x\geq 1$): $g(x)=2x-3 \to 2(1)-3=-1$.

Approaching from the left ($x<1$): $g(x)=x-2 \to 1-2=-1$.

Since the function approaches the same value from both sides, the limit **exists** and equals $-1$.
:::

## Rules for differentiation

5. Find $f'(x)$ for $f(x)=x^7$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
f'(x)=7x^6
$$
:::

6. Find $f'(x)$ for $f(x)=\sqrt[4]{x}$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
f(x)=x^{1/4} \Rightarrow f'(x)=\frac{1}{4}x^{-3/4}
$$
:::

7. Find $y'$ for $y=x^4+3x^2-20$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
y'=4x^3+6x
$$
:::

8. Find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for $y=4x^4-\frac{7}{x^3}+9$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=16x^3+\frac{21}{x^4}
$$
:::

9. Find $k'(t)$ for $k(t)=4t^{2/3}-5\ln(t)$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
k'(t)=\frac{8}{3}t^{-1/3}-\frac{5}{t}
$$
:::

## Higher-order and Partial Derivatives

10. Find the third derivative of $K(w)=w^6+5w^4-3w^2+w$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
K'(w)=6w^5+20w^3-6w+1
$$
$$
K''(w)=30w^4+60w^2-6
$$
$$
K'''(w)=120w^3+120w
$$
:::

11. Position is given by $s(t)=t^3-6t^2+9t$. Find the velocity function $s'(t)$ and the acceleration function $s''(t)$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
v(t)=s'(t)=3t^2-12t+9
$$
$$
a(t)=s''(t)=6t-12
$$
:::

12. Find $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}$ and $\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ for $f(x,y)=3xy^2-x^2+5y-2$, then evaluate both at $(2,1)$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}=3y^2-2x, \qquad \frac{\partial f}{\partial y}=6xy+5
$$
At $(2,1)$: $\left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\right|_{(2,1)}=3(1)^2-2(2)=-1$, and $\left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}\right|_{(2,1)}=6(2)(1)+5=17$
:::

13. Find $\frac{\partial C}{\partial x}$, $\frac{\partial C}{\partial y}$, and $\frac{\partial C}{\partial z}$ for $C(x,y,z)=2x^2z-5y^3+3xy-z^2+10$

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution
$$
\frac{\partial C}{\partial x}=4xz+3y, \qquad \frac{\partial C}{\partial y}=-15y^2+3x, \qquad \frac{\partial C}{\partial z}=2x^2-2z
$$
:::
